narrative: 一张脸和一片未被使用的空白矩形，本身就可以构成一整场戏。我们在等待那个目标物的出现：一个进门的人、一幅画、一扇庭院窗户。
主体并不拥有这份剩余空间，未见之物才拥有它。
当画面中没有真正的“看”这个动作时，这就不是对的工具。一张直视镜头的脸旁边的空白空间，并不算视线空间，
那只是剩余空间而已。如果你需要那个目标物出现在画面中，就把它放进去，不要再假装那片空气是一个谜。
视线空间是一种构图。主观视角的剪辑衔接才是这项构图的完成，
你也可以只保留这份凝视而从不给出回应，那是另一种残忍。
how: 除非你是在做短边构图，否则应在凝视方向留出比头后方更多的画面空间。如果下一个镜头是那个目标物，就匹配好视线的高度和方向。
侧脸或四分之三侧脸能让这份被“拥有”的空间显得一目了然。除非“竞争”本身就是重点，否则不要用相互竞争的脸孔填满那片区域。
提示词：Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see.
when: 当被注视的对象位于画外，或即将进入画面时使用它：一个观察者、一位画家、一个狙击手、一个站在门口的爱人。不要在一次面对镜头的采访旁边留出死气沉沉的空白，就称之为一种“凝视”。
vs: 前导空间（Lead Room）涵盖了运动因素以及步行时的经典礼节。视线空间则特指目光本身，尤其是朝向画外目标物的目光。
主观镜头（Point of View）是他们所看之物的镜头。视线空间则是他们“正在看”这个动作本身的镜头。
短边构图（Short Siding）剥夺了这片空间。反应镜头（Reaction Shot）如果这张脸本身就是整个事件，可能几乎不需要留出这样的空间。
框中框（Frame within Frame）可以把目标物放进视线空间之中的一扇窗户里。
examples_film: 《后窗》（Rear Window）先建立杰夫（Jeff）的目光，再用庭院中的活动来回应它；《燃烧女子的肖像》（Portrait of a Lady on Fire）把“看”本身当作主体，画家与模特之间的空间才是真正的场域。
《斯坦达尔综合症》（The Stendhal Syndrome）把安娜的目光与博物馆中的画作一一对应。这是关于视线方向的语法，而不是一个可以照搬的游客视角。
mistakes: 最常见的误用是剩余的壁纸空间，或一次虚假的视线匹配剪辑。破绽是脸的错误一侧留有空白，或者下一个镜头在几何上根本不可能是这个目光所能触及的方向。
修正方法：把剩余空间放在凝视方向上，并在完成这个视线剪辑衔接时匹配好高度和角度。

faq.q: 电影中的视线空间（Look Space）是什么？
faq.a: 它是目光所拥有的画面区域，通常位于眼睛前方。重要的目标物往往位于画外，因此这片空气本身就是一种张力。在剪辑中，这个“看”的镜头可能会衔接上一个展示所见之物的镜头。

faq.q: 视线空间（Look Space）与前导空间（Lead Room）有何区别？
faq.a: 前导空间是运动方向上的空间，延伸开来也包括一次静止的凝视。视线空间则是目光作为一种与某个物体（无论存在与否）之间的关系。它们在一个静止的侧脸镜头中会有所重叠，但并非同一项任务：一个奔跑的人需要前导空间，一个眺望庭院的观察者需要视线空间。

faq.q: 什么时候该用视线空间（Look Space）？
faq.a: 当重要的事物位于画外或即将出现，而正在注视的这张脸就是当下时态时使用它。不要把一次采访镜头中剩余的边角空白误当作一种“凝视”。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写视线空间（Look Space）的提示词？
faq.a: 让眼睛指向某个方向，并清空那个方向的画面区域。示例：Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see。说明目标物不在画面中。对于视频，你可以额外添加一个主观镜头作为回应。

narrative: A face and a rectangle of unused air can be a whole scene. We wait for the object: a person entering, a painting, a courtyard window.
The subject does not own the surplus. The unseen does.
It is the wrong tool when there is no look. Empty space beside a face that stares into lens is not look-space.
It is leftover. If you need the object on-screen, put it there and stop pretending the air is a mystery.
Look-space is the composition. The POV cut is the completion.
You can hold the look and never pay off, which is a different cruelty.
how: Place more frame in the gaze direction than behind the head, unless you are short-siding. Match the height and direction of the look if the next shot is the object.
A profile or three-quarter makes the owned field obvious. Do not fill that field with competing faces unless the competition is the point.
Prompt: Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see.
when: Use it when the object of attention is off-screen or about to enter: a watcher, a painter, a sniper, a lover at a door. Do not leave dead air beside a to-camera interview and call it a look.
vs: Lead Room includes motion and classical manners for a walk. Look-space is specifically the gaze, especially toward an off-screen object.
Point of View is the shot of what they see. Look-space is the shot of them seeing.
Short Siding withholds this field. Reaction Shot may be a look with almost no space if the face is the whole event.
Frame within Frame can put the object in a window inside the look-space.
examples_film: Rear Window builds Jeff's looks and then pays them with courtyard activity. Portrait of a Lady on Fire makes looking the subject, space between painter and model as the true field.
The Stendhal Syndrome matches Anna's looks to museum paintings. Grammar of eyeline, not a tourist view to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is leftover wallpaper, or a false eyeline cut. The tell is empty space on the wrong side of the face, or a next shot the look could not geometrically reach.
The fix is to put the surplus in the gaze direction and to match height and angle if you complete the look.

faq.q: What is look space in film?
faq.a: It is the area of frame a gaze owns, usually ahead of the eyes. Often the important object is off-screen, so the air is tension. In editing, the look may be joined to a shot of what is seen.

Lead room is space in the direction of movement, and by extension a standing look. Look space is the gaze as a relationship to an object, present or withheld. A runner needs lead room. A watcher of a courtyard needs look-space. They overlap in a still profile. They are not the same job.

faq.q: When should I use look space?
faq.a: Use it when what matters is off-screen or about to arrive, and the face watching is the present tense. Do not confuse leftover margin on an interview with a look.

faq.q: How do I prompt look space for AI image or video?
faq.a: Point the eyes and empty the field they face. Example: Generous look space for [Subject], the off-screen gaze owning a field of air, tension in what we cannot see. Say the object is not in frame. For video, you can add a second shot as POV.
